# Notation and reading guide

*Fits.* REML: the ordinary penalized fit; NCV: the same model with smoothing parameters
chosen by curve-blocked neighbourhood cross-validation (one curve left out at a time).
*Intervals.* model-based: the fit's own Bayesian covariance; CL2: curve-clustered
sandwich covariance with the exact Bell–McCaffrey leverage adjustment; bias-aware: the NCV
fit's CL2 interval widened in quadrature by the NCV–REML difference δ; hybrid: the NCV
estimate with the REML fit's CL2 standard error; AR(1): a working AR(1) error model with
ρ profiled (definitions in @sec-dgp and @sec-ar1-fit). *Recipes.* REML + CL2 (the recommended recipe; "fallback" in the
recommendation rule) and NCV + CL2 + bias allowance ("proposal"). *Estimands.* the
conditional mean E(Y | X) of a frozen test cohort on the response scale, the bivariate
coefficient surface β(s,t) of the functional covariate term ff(X) (or f(x,t) of a
scalar-covariate smooth), the functional intercept α(t) and the scalar-covariate effect
γ(t). *Coverage* is the average over the evaluation grid of pointwise 95% intervals; the
5% quantile of pointwise coverage is the lower tail over grid points. *CE* (calibration
error): root-mean-square undercoverage over a pool of cells with each cell's Monte Carlo
variance subtracted; a recipe is adequate if CE ≤ 2 pp. *Rule classes* per dataset: P =
proposal, F = fallback, E = practically equivalent (simpler recipe), N = neither adequate,
U = unresolved (a bootstrap interval straddles a threshold; by the rule an N is
never downgraded to U, so running and DTI β are N although their fallback CE intervals
straddle 2 pp); question 1: C = CL2 beats model-based by ≥ 2 pp. "Dependent" synthetic cells have the rough (OU) or smooth (DTI-FPC)
error process; "core" cells form the family × error × G × signal factorial.

*Interval score.* For a 95% interval $[l, u]$ and truth $y$ the score is
$(u - l) + \frac{2}{0.05}\{(l - y)\,1(y < l) + (y - u)\,1(y > u)\}$, averaged over grid points and replicates: a proper scoring rule that rewards narrow intervals and
penalises each miss in proportion to its distance from the interval. *Relative error* of an estimate:
√(grid mean of (estimate − truth)² / grid mean of truth²), the truth centred at its grid mean for the mean and α(t);
*detection*: the share of grid points with |truth| > 25% of max |truth| where the interval excludes zero on the
side of the truth (@sec-relerr).

*Interval-score ratios* (bias-aware or hybrid vs REML + CL2, proposal vs fallback) are
always the geometric mean over the cells concerned of the per-cell ratio of mean interval
scores, the definition used by the recommendation rule; widths likewise.

*Monte Carlo precision.* Every cell has `r unique(S$n_rep)` replicates. The stored MC SE of a
grid-average coverage is `r rng_pp(se_dep_cl2, 2)` for REML + CL2 and `r rng_pp(se_dep_model, 2)`
for the model-based intervals in the dependent core cells at G = 100 (plasmode REML + CL2:
`r rng_pp(se_plas_cl2, 2)`); the grid average is far more precise than a single grid
point, whose binomial SE near 0.95 is `r pp(sqrt(0.95 * 0.05 / 200))`. Bootstrap intervals
in brackets are 95% replicate-bootstrap intervals of pooled or paired quantities.

# Summary of findings

```{r summary-relerr}
# relative error and interval informativeness (details: @sec-relerr and the plasmode subsection)
rel_s <- read_summary("final", "relative-error") |>
  left_join(S |> distinct(cell, error), by = "cell") |>
  filter(estimand == "beta", error != "iid")
rs_med <- \(a, col) median(rel_s[[col]][rel_s$arm == a])
rel_p <- read_summary("plasmode", "relative-error") |>
  filter(estimand == "beta", flip == "curve", G > 40, error == "attached") |>
  group_by(app, arm) |>
  summarise(rel = median(rel_rmse_median), det = median(detect), .groups = "drop")
rp <- \(a, col) rel_p[[col]][rel_p$arm == a]
# comparators, NCV-centred corrections, smoothing-parameter term, cost (details: @sec-comparators, @sec-ncv-intervals, @sec-lambda, @sec-timing)
cmp_set <- \(d) mutate(d, setting = case_when(source == "plasmode" ~ "plasmode", error == "iid" ~ "synthetic, independent", TRUE ~ "synthetic, dependent"))
s_cmp <- readr::read_csv("comparators/summaries/comparators-cells.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> cmp_set()
s_ca <- readr::read_csv("comparators/summaries/cl2-arms-cells.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(window == "1-100") |> cmp_set()
s_cv <- \(d, a, set, e = "beta") d$coverage[d$arm == a & d$setting == set & d$estimand == e]
s_cmp_mse <- s_cmp |> filter(estimand == "beta", setting == "synthetic, dependent", arm %in% c("pcre", "gls_fpc")) |>
  select(cell, arm, mse) |>
  left_join(S |> filter(arm == "ncv_cl2", estimand == "beta") |> select(cell, mse_ncv = mse), by = "cell")
s_pm_keys <- read_summary("plasmode", "ncv-diag-cells") |> distinct(cell, app)
s_comb <- readr::read_csv("ncv-rbc/summaries/combo2-pm-cells.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  left_join(s_pm_keys, by = "cell") |> filter(estimand == "beta", arm == "rbc_p_ij", !is.na(app)) |>
  group_by(app) |> summarise(coverage = mean(coverage), .groups = "drop")
s_lc <- readr::read_csv("lambda-correction/summaries/lc-cells.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(crit == "z", estimand == "beta", error != "iid", arm %in% c("cl2", "ij_lin")) |>
  group_by(cell) |> mutate(score_rel = score / score[arm == "cl2"]) |> ungroup()
s_tim <- \(m, col = "fit_time") median(TIMING[[col]][TIMING$method == m], na.rm = TRUE)
s_cmpf <- readr::read_csv("comparators/summaries/comparators-fits.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(startsWith(key, "p"))
s_boot_time <- median(s_cmpf$time[s_cmpf$arm == "BOOT"])
# REML + CL2 in the same plasmode comparator cells: fit time plus the CL2 time stored in `info`
s_remlcl2_time <- median(s_cmpf$time[s_cmpf$arm == "REML"] + as.numeric(sub(".*cl2_time=([0-9.eE+-]+).*", "\\1", s_cmpf$info[s_cmpf$arm == "REML"])))
```

1. **Model-based intervals fail under within-curve dependence; curve-clustered CL2 on the
   REML fit repairs them.** Synthetic: in the `r n_distinct(core_dep$cell)` dependent core
   cells at G = 100 the model-based intervals cover `r rng(cov_of(core_dep, "reml_model"))`
   for the mean and β; REML + CL2 covers `r rng(cov_of(core_dep, "reml_cl2"))`. On a four
   times denser grid model-based coverage of β falls by a further
   `r rng_pp(-dense$estimate[dense$value == "coverage_reml_model" & dense$error != "iid"])`
   while REML + CL2 moves by at most `r pp(max(abs(dense$estimate[dense$value == "coverage_reml_cl2" & dense$error != "iid"])))`.
   Under independent errors at G = 100 CL2 costs at most `r pp(max(Q1$estimate[Q1$name == "iid_cost_reml"]))`
   of coverage (at G = 40 up to `r pp(max(iid40_cost$cost))`, binary mean). This holds in
   the synthetic study for six response families, four estimands and both term types.
   Plasmode (Gaussian, ff model only): pooled model-based coverage `r rng(pmc("reml_model"))`
   on the six counted datasets and `r rng(pms("reml_model"))` on the three stress tests;
   REML + CL2 `r rng(pmc("reml_cl2"))` and `r rng(pms("reml_cl2"))`. *Against it:* REML + CL2
   covers binary α(t) and γ(t) at `r rng(bin_ag$coverage_mean[bin_ag$arm == "reml_cl2"])`
   (model-based `r rng(bin_ag$coverage_mean[bin_ag$arm == "reml_model" & bin_ag$error == "iid"])`
   under iid; for α(t) partly a link-scale bias of the GLM intercept, studentised mean
   `r rng(za_bin_core$z_mean_cl2, 2)` under dependence), the misregistered Poisson mean at `r rng(warp_pois$coverage_mean[warp_pois$arm == "reml_cl2"])`
   (every recipe undercovers there), and its lower tail for the mean at G = 40 under iid
   errors is `r f(min(q05_of(core_iid40, "reml_cl2")))`.

2. **The limits of REML + CL2.** On the counted datasets its β intervals are
   `r rng_pp(LEVEL - pmc("reml_cl2", "beta"))` short of nominal (stress tests
   `r rng_pp(LEVEL - pms("reml_cl2", "beta"))`), its 5% pointwise quantile is
   `r rng(pm_counted$q05_mean[pm_counted$arm == "reml_cl2" & pm_counted$estimand == "beta"])`
   for β (synthetic dependent cells at G = 100: `r rng(q05_of(core_dep, "reml_cl2"))`), and at
   G = 40 it loses a further `r rng_pp(g40_app$loss[g40_app$arm == "reml_cl2" & g40_app$role == "counted"])`
   (synthetic dependent cells: `r rng(cov_of(core_dep40, "reml_cl2"))` at G = 40 vs
   `r rng(cov_of(core_dep, "reml_cl2"))` at G = 100). *Against it:* under REML-fitted truths
   the lower tail on running, DTI and electricity is `r rng(bt("reml_cl2", "REML", col = "q05")[by_truth$app[by_truth$arm == "reml_cl2" & by_truth$truth == "REML" & by_truth$estimand == "beta"] %in% c("running", "dti", "adelaide")], 3)`.
   A curve-robust term for the uncertainty of the selected smoothing parameters raises REML + CL2's β coverage in
   the dependent synthetic core cells from `r f(mean(s_lc$coverage[s_lc$arm == "cl2"]))` to
   `r f(mean(s_lc$coverage[s_lc$arm == "ij_lin"]))` at an interval score `r f(exp(mean(log(s_lc$score_rel[s_lc$arm == "ij_lin"]))), 3)`
   times CL2's (@sec-lambda).

3. **Estimation: curve-blocked NCV improves the bivariate surface under dependent errors
   in the synthetic study; in the plasmode study the gain depends on the truth source.**
   Synthetic, dependent core cells at G = 100: NCV/REML
   MSE ratio for β `r rng(ratio_of(r_dep, "beta"))`, mean `r rng(ratio_of(r_dep, "mean"))`,
   γ(t) `r rng(ratio_of(r_dep, "gamma"))`, α(t) `r rng(ratio_of(r_dep, "alpha"))`; under
   independent errors `r rng(ratio_of(r_iid, "beta"))` for β. Plasmode (geometric mean over
   residual sources, G = all): β `r rng(rt("NCV", "beta"))` under the NCV-fitted truth,
   `r rng(rt("MID", "beta"))` under the log-midpoint truth, `r rng(rt("REML", "beta"))` under
   the REML-fitted truth (NCV-derived truths align the target with the NCV fit; the weather
   data, where NCV is rougher than REML yet wins under all truths, show that this is not a
   pure smoothness mechanism). *Against it:* NCV loses for β under the REML-fitted truth on
   `r sum(rt("REML", "beta") > 1)` of 9 datasets, and the plasmode gains on α(t) reach
   `r f(min(rt("NCV", "alpha")), 2)` on one dataset, so the gain is not confined to surfaces there.

4. **Bias-aware NCV intervals and the NCV/REML hybrid are not reliably calibrated.** The
   allowance inherits REML's noise (β coverage `r rng(S$coverage_mean[S$block == "basis_size" & S$basis == "xlarge" & S$error == "fpc" & S$estimand == "beta" & S$arm == "ncv_cl2_bias"], 3)`
   with the largest bases, width `r rng(width_ratio$bias_aware[width_ratio$block == "basis_size" & width_ratio$basis == "xlarge" & width_ratio$error == "fpc" & width_ratio$estimand == "beta"], 2)`
   times REML + CL2's) and cannot see bias shared by both fits: under real REML-fitted truths
   its β coverage on the counted plasmode datasets is `r rng(bt("ncv_cl2_bias", "REML", role_sel = "counted"))`
   (`r rng(bt("ncv_cl2_bias", "NCV", role_sel = "counted"))` under NCV-fitted truths), the
   shortfall sitting at the truth's curvature peaks. Averaged over all nine datasets, under REML-fitted truths the hybrid is
   worse than REML + CL2 on every metric (β coverage `r f(hv2s("cov hybrid", "REML"))` vs
   `r f(hv2s("cov REML+CL2", "REML"))`, 5% quantile `r f(hyb_q05_reml, 2)` vs `r f(cl2_q05_reml, 2)`,
   interval score `r f(hv2s("IS hybrid/REML+CL2", "REML"), 2)` times); it is better only under
   NCV- and MID-derived truths, partly by overcovering (`r f(hv2s("cov hybrid", "NCV"))`,
   `r f(hv2s("cov hybrid", "MID"))`). *Against it:* the
   recommendation rule with the undercoverage-only criterion selects the bias-aware proposal
   for both estimands in all three families on the synthetic pool (interval-score ratios
   `r rng(REC$score_ratio[REC$proposal == "ncv_cl2_bias"])`); on the plasmode datasets it
   does not (@sec-rule, @sec-plasmode-rule). Corrections of the NCV-centred interval do not change this on real
   data: the one-step bias correction combined with the smoothing-parameter term covers β at
   `r rng(s_comb$coverage)` per plasmode dataset (@sec-ncv-intervals, @sec-lambda).

5. **AR(1) working models fail in the plasmode study:** `r rng(ar1_main$coverage_mean)` for the mean
   and β on the nine plasmode datasets (real covariates and residual curves, frozen fitted truths) (log-midpoint truth, REML residuals; synthetic misregistration:
   mean `r rng(ar1_s$coverage_mean[ar1_s$error == "warp" & ar1_s$estimand == "mean"])`, β
   `r rng(ar1_s$coverage_mean[ar1_s$error == "warp" & ar1_s$estimand == "beta"])`). *Against
   it:* on stationary homoskedastic synthetic errors AR(1) is conservative and competitive
   (`r rng(ar1_s$coverage_mean[ar1_s$error %in% c("ou", "fpc", "ou0", "osc")])`).

6. **Under within-curve dependence the REML estimate of β is poor, so REML + CL2 is valid but much
   less informative there.** Synthetic dependent cells: median relative error (√ of mean squared error over
   mean squared truth) of β `r f(rs_med("reml_cl2", "rel_rmse_median"), 2)` for REML vs
   `r f(rs_med("ncv_cl2", "rel_rmse_median"), 2)` for NCV; REML + CL2 half-widths are
   `r f(rs_med("reml_cl2", "rel_halfwidth_median"), 2)` times the effect's size and detect
   `r f(rs_med("reml_cl2", "detect"), 2)` of the clearly non-zero grid points (NCV + CL2:
   `r f(rs_med("ncv_cl2", "rel_halfwidth_median"), 2)`, `r f(rs_med("ncv_cl2", "detect"), 2)`). The REML/NCV gap
   is present at every signal level (largest at low signal). Plasmode: relative error of β `r rng(rp("reml_cl2", "rel"))` (REML) and
   `r rng(rp("ncv_cl2", "rel"))` (NCV) per dataset; REML + CL2 detects `r rng(rp("reml_cl2", "det"))`.
   *Against it:* NCV-centred intervals do not cover reliably (item 4), so the better estimate comes
   without a calibrated interval. All metrics side by side, with interval scores: @sec-metrics.

7. **Modelling the residual covariance (pcre, GLS) does not replace CL2 on real residual curves; the curve
   bootstrap covers at a much higher cost.** Under dependent
   synthetic errors the pcre curve effect and GLS with an FPCA residual covariance cover β at
   `r rng(s_cv(s_cmp, "pcre", "synthetic, dependent"))` and `r rng(s_cv(s_cmp, "gls_fpc", "synthetic, dependent"))`; on the
   plasmode comparator cells at `r rng(s_cv(s_cmp, "pcre", "plasmode"))` and `r rng(s_cv(s_cmp, "gls_fpc", "plasmode"))`, against
   `r rng(s_cv(s_cmp, "reml_cl2", "plasmode"))` for REML + CL2. CL2 on the GLS or pcre fit covers β at
   `r rng(s_cv(s_ca, "gls_fpc_cl2", "plasmode"))` and `r rng(s_cv(s_ca, "pcre_cl2", "plasmode"))` there (@sec-comp-cl2); GLS with
   the raw residual covariance undercovers even under independent errors (`r rng(s_cv(s_cmp, "gls_raw", "synthetic, independent"))`);
   the curve bootstrap (percentile, 199 refits) covers `r rng(s_cv(s_cmp, "boot_pct", "plasmode"))` on the plasmode cells at a
   median of `r f(s_boot_time, 0)` s per data set (@sec-comparators, @sec-timing). *Against it:* on dependent synthetic data pcre and GLS (FPCA) cover β like REML + CL2
   (`r rng(s_cv(s_cmp, "reml_cl2", "synthetic, dependent"))`) and estimate it with an MSE
   `r rng(s_cmp_mse$mse / s_cmp_mse$mse_ncv)` times NCV's.

8. **Cost.** Gaussian, G = 100, one core: REML fit `r f(s_tim("REML"), 1)` s plus `r f(s_tim("REML", "cl2_time"), 1)` s for
   CL2; curve-blocked NCV fit `r f(s_tim("NCV"), 1)` s; AR(1) with ρ profiled `r f(s_tim("AR1"), 0)` s (@sec-timing).

# Synthetic study

## Design

```{r design-table}
blocks <- DESIGN |>
  mutate(fitted = if_else(family == fit_family, FAMILY_LABELS[family], paste0(FAMILY_LABELS[family], " (fitted as ", FAMILY_LABELS[fit_family], ")"))) |>
  group_by(block) |>
  summarise(
    cells = n(),
    families = paste(unique(fitted), collapse = ", "),
    errors = paste(unique(SHORT_ERROR[error]), collapse = ", "),
    G = paste(sort(unique(G)), collapse = ", "),
    signal = paste(unique(signal), collapse = ", "),
    truth = paste(unique(truth), collapse = ", "),
    D = paste(unique(D), collapse = ", "),
    model = paste(unique(c(M1 = "ff(X)", M2 = "f(x,t)")[model]), collapse = ", "),
    covariate = paste(unique(covariate), collapse = ", "),
    basis = paste(unique(basis), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(match(block, c("core", "warp", "dense_grid", "rough_truth", "term_type", "families", "ar1_home", "oscillating", "warp_ar1", "heteroskedastic", "lowrank_covariate", "basis_size")))
save_tab(blocks, "synthetic-design-blocks")
fit_summary <- FITS |>
  group_by(fit_family, fit) |>
  summarise(converged = weighted.mean(converged, n), median_time_s = median(median_time), .groups = "drop")
save_tab(fit_summary, "synthetic-fits")
```

The synthetic study has `r nrow(DESIGN)` cells in `r nrow(blocks)` blocks
(@tbl-design), `r unique(S$n_rep)` replicates each, `r sum(FITS$n[FITS$fit == "REML"])`
tasks, none failed. Each cell fits the model by REML and by curve-blocked NCV and scores
the conditional mean of a frozen test cohort, the surface β(s,t) (or f(x,t)), α(t) and
γ(t). Every cell uses the same random draws per replicate, so contrasts between cells
are paired. NCV fits converged in `r f(100 * fit_summary$converged[fit_summary$fit == "NCV" & fit_summary$fit_family == "gaussian"], 1)`%
of Gaussian tasks; the scaled-t family's NCV "non-convergence"
(`r f(100 * fit_summary$converged[fit_summary$fit == "NCV" & fit_summary$fit_family == "scat"], 0)`% converged)
is a flat optimum, not a wrong fit (refits from different starts agree to
< `r formatC(max(SCAT$beta_max_diff), format = "e", digits = 0)` in the coefficients).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-design
#| tbl-cap: "Blocks of the synthetic design. Errors: iid = independent; OU = rough stationary (OU kernel with nugget); smooth = curves from the DTI residual FPCs; AR(1) = exact AR(1); sign-chg. = damped cosine with sign-changing correlation; var(t) / var(z) / var(t,z) = the smooth process with a variance profile along t / a subject scale depending on the scalar covariate / both; misreg. = misregistration."
show(blocks |> select(block, cells, families, errors, G, signal, truth, D, model, covariate, basis))
```

### Data-generating process {#sec-dgp}

*Models.* For curves i = 1, …, G and the family's link g:
M1 (default) $g\{\mathrm E\,Y_i(t)\} = \alpha(t) + \int X_i(s)\beta(s,t)\,ds + z_i\gamma(t)$ with $z_i \sim N(0, 1)$;
M2 (term-type block) $g\{\mathrm E\,Y_i(t)\} = \alpha(t) + f(x_i, t) + z_i\gamma(t)$ with $x_i \sim U(0, 1)$, a smooth effect of a
scalar covariate that varies over t. pffr fits f with $\sum_i \hat f(x_i, t) = 0$ at every t, so f is scored against its truth
centred on each data set's own $x_i$, and α is not scored in M2.

*Grids.* Responses are generated on `r length(CONST$T_DENSE)` equidistant points in t ∈ [0, 1] and the functional
covariate on `r length(CONST$S_GRID)` points in s; the fitted grid keeps every fourth t point (D = 61) or all of them
(D = 241, dense-grid block), so the grids are nested. Estimands are evaluated on fixed coarser grids, identical for
every D: `r length(CONST$EVAL_T)` points in t, `r length(CONST$EVAL_S)` in s (β), `r length(CONST$EVAL_X)` points
x ∈ [0.05, 0.95] (f), and the conditional mean for the `r CONST$N_TEST` curves of a frozen test cohort at the
`r length(CONST$EVAL_T)` t points.

*Covariate.* $X_i(s) = \xi_{i0} + \sum_{j=1}^{29} \xi_{ij}\sqrt 2\cos(j\pi s)$, $\xi_{ij} \sim N(0, (j+1)^{-2})$; the constant term keeps the
s-constant part of β identified. The centred spectrum has a first-PC share of 62%, 88% for the first four and a
99.5% rank of 24 (close to the DTI covariate's 67%, 86% and 26). The low-rank variant uses variances (j+1)⁻³ (99.5%
rank 9, below 1.5 times the ff basis's s-dimension, like the running data's knee angle).

*Truths.* $\beta(s,t) = \cos(\pi s)\sin(\pi t) + (s - \tfrac12)\cos(2\pi t)$; $f(x,t) = 2(x - \tfrac12)\cos(\pi t) + \sin(\pi x)\,t$;
$\gamma(t) = \sin(2\pi t)$; the rough ("wiggly") truth adds $0.6\sin(3\pi s)\sin(3\pi t)$ to β (and f) and $0.5\sin(5\pi t)$ to γ. Each truth is projected by
least squares (on `r CONST$PROJECTION_N` points per axis) onto the fitted default bases, so it is exactly representable;
the misspecification experiment (@sec-misspec) relaxes this. The truths are scaled so that the non-intercept signal
$S = \int \mathrm{Var}_{X,z}\{\eta(t) - \alpha(t)\}\,dt$ splits `r 100 * CONST$SIGNAL_SHARE_MAIN`% / `r 100 * (1 - CONST$SIGNAL_SHARE_MAIN)`% between the
main term and γ, and multiplied by √S. α(t) is a Gaussian bump (centre `r CONST$BUMP_CENTER`, sd `r CONST$BUMP_SD`,
height √S), projected onto the intercept basis, plus a constant that sets each GLM's average response level
(found by root search on a population sample of `r CONST$N_POPULATION` covariate draws).

*Signal and families.* Gaussian: error variance set for R² ∈ {0.2, 0.5, 0.8}. Poisson: √S ∈ {0.5, 1} on the
log scale, average mean count `r CONST$MEAN_LEVEL[["poisson"]]`. Binary (Bernoulli per grid point): √S ∈ {0.5, 1} on the
logit scale, average prevalence `r CONST$MEAN_LEVEL[["binomial"]]`. Extended families: scaled t with `r CONST$SCAT_DF` df
(as Gaussian at R² 0.5), beta (φ = `r CONST$BETAR_PHI`, average mean `r CONST$MEAN_LEVEL[["betar"]]`) and negative binomial
(size `r CONST$NB_SIZE`, average mean `r CONST$MEAN_LEVEL[["nb"]]`, also fitted as Poisson) at √S = 0.5. The default level is
R² 0.5 for Gaussian and √S 0.5 otherwise.

*Within-curve dependence.* A zero-mean process $Z_i \sim N(0, R)$ with correlation kernel R on the grid is scaled for
Gaussian errors or used as the latent layer of a Gaussian copula for the other families,
$Y_{ij} = F_{ij}^{-1}(\Phi(Z_{ij}))$, so every marginal is exactly the fitted family with mean $g^{-1}(\eta_{ij})$ and the working-independence
model is wrong only about the dependence.

| error process | kernel R(s, t) | role |
|---|---|---|
| iid | 1{s = t} | control |
| OU | `r 1 - CONST$OU_NUGGET` exp(−\|s − t\|/`r CONST$OU_RANGE`) + `r CONST$OU_NUGGET`·1{s = t} (Gaussian design effect 8 at D = 61) | rough, stationary |
| smooth | residual covariance of the DTI application (`rcst ~ ff(cca)`, 92 curves) by FPCA: 24 eigenfunctions plus 6% white noise, standardised to a correlation (design effect 11.8 at D = 61, 47 at D = 241) | smooth, realistic |
| AR(1) | exp(−\|s − t\|/`r CONST$OU0_RANGE`), exactly AR(1) on the grid | the AR(1) model's own case |
| sign-changing | `r 1 - CONST$OSC_NUGGET` exp(−\|s − t\|/`r CONST$OSC_RANGE`) cos(2π\|s − t\|/`r CONST$OSC_PERIOD`) + `r CONST$OSC_NUGGET`·1{s = t} | stationary, correlations change sign with lag |
| var(t), var(z), var(t,z) | the smooth process with the DTI variance profile along t (variances 0.46–2.42, average 1); with subject i's errors scaled by exp(`r CONST$HET_SD` z_i − `r CONST$HET_SD^2`); both | heteroskedastic (Gaussian) |
| misregistration | below | phase variability |

*Misregistration.* The model holds on each curve's own clock and is observed on the common clock:
$Y_i(t_j) = \eta_i(h_i(t_j)) + \varepsilon_i(h_i(t_j))$ with $h_i(t) = t + a_i\sin(\pi t)/\pi$, $a_i \sim N(0, `r CONST$WARP_SD`^2)$
truncated at $|a_i| \le `r CONST$WARP_MAX`$ (monotone warps with fixed endpoints, maximal displacement SD 10%) and iid ε. For Gaussian
responses the common-clock coefficients are the smeared functions $\tilde\alpha(t) = \mathrm E_h\,\alpha(h(t))$, $\tilde\beta(s,t) = \mathrm E_h\,\beta(s, h(t))$,
$\tilde\gamma(t) = \mathrm E_h\,\gamma(h(t))$ (quadrature over a with `r CONST$WARP_QUAD_N` nodes), and every estimand is scored against them;
for GLMs the observed-clock mean is not $g^{-1}$ of a linear predictor, so GLM misregistration cells score only the
test-cohort mean, against its exact quadrature. These cells run at high signal.

*Fits.* Every data set is fitted by `pffr()` (refund) with mgcv's `gam()` twice: by REML and by NCV with each curve
as one leave-out block. Bases: cubic P-splines (mgcv `ps`, m = (2, 1), i.e. first-order difference penalties); intercept and
γ(t) k = `r CONST$BASIS_T$k`; ff term `r CONST$BASIS_FF$k[1]` (s) × `r CONST$BASIS_FF$k[2]` (t); M2's f(x, t)
`r CONST$BASIS_X$k` (x) × `r CONST$BASIS_T$k` (t) with the x knots fixed to [0, 1]; in the basis-size block
`r CONST$BASES$large$t$k` and `r CONST$BASES$large$ff$k[1]` × `r CONST$BASES$large$ff$k[2]` (large) or
`r CONST$BASES$xlarge$t$k` and `r CONST$BASES$xlarge$ff$k[1]` × `r CONST$BASES$xlarge$ff$k[2]` (xlarge), nested spline spaces.
Extra fits: pointwise NCV (mgcv's default neighbourhoods; Gaussian core cells at G = 100 with iid and smooth errors,
and the Gaussian sign-changing cell) and the AR(1) working model (@sec-ar1-fit).

*Intervals.* All intervals are pointwise at nominal 95%, estimate ± 1.96 SE, for an estimand Lθ (rows of the
lpmatrix for the mean, the term's basis at the evaluation points for β, f, α, γ; the inverse link applied to the
interval ends for the mean): model-based (the REML fit's Bayesian covariance with mgcv's smoothing-parameter correction, V_c; V_p for NCV fits,
whose V_c is not a valid covariance in the mgcv build used), CL2 (curve-clustered sandwich with the exact Bell–McCaffrey adjustment of
each curve's residual block, Bayesian form V_p − V_e added), bias-aware (NCV + CL2 widened in quadrature by
δ = L(θ̂_NCV − θ̂_REML)), its variant on the frequentist CL2, the hybrid (NCV estimate with REML + CL2's SE) and the AR(1)
fit's model-based interval.

*Replicates.* R = `r CONST$N_REP` per cell. Replicate r uses seed `r CONST$SEED_BASE` + r in every cell, and all draws are
made at full size (G = `r CONST$G_MAX` curves, dense grid; G = 40 uses the first 40 curves, D = 61 the nested
subgrid), so all cells share their random draws (common random numbers) and contrasts between cells are paired by
replicate. The test cohort (`r CONST$N_TEST` covariate draws, seed `r CONST$SEED_TEST`) is the same in every cell.
Software: refund `pffr-refactor` commit `r substr(CONST$REFUND_SHA_EXPECTED, 1, 8)` and mgcv `r CONST$MGCV_VERSION`
(pre-release), both asserted in every task.

## Inference

### Model-based intervals versus CL2 by family and dependence

```{r fig-coverage-core}
#| fig-cap: "Coverage of the conditional mean and of the coefficient surface in the core cells at the default signal level, by family, error process and number of curves. Points are grid-averaged coverages, bars ± 2 Monte Carlo SE, the dashed line the nominal 0.95."
#| fig-height: 5.5
d <- S |>
  filter(block == "core", signal == "mid", estimand %in% c("mean", "beta"), arm %in% MAIN_ARMS) |>
  mutate(arm = label_arm(arm), estimand = label_estimand(estimand), error = label_error(error), family = label_family(family), G = paste0("G = ", G))
fig <- coverage_plot(d, "error", vars(G, estimand), vars(family))
save_fig(fig, "coverage-core", 6.5, 5.5)
fig
```

```{r q1-table}
q1 <- Q1 |>
  mutate(value = ci(estimate, lower, upper)) |>
  select(family, estimand, name, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = value) |>
  rename(`CE model-based (REML)` = ce_reml_model, `CE REML + CL2` = ce_reml_cl2, `CE model-based (NCV)` = ce_ncv_model, `CE NCV + CL2` = ce_ncv_cl2, `gain REML` = ce_gain_reml, `gain NCV` = ce_gain_ncv, `iid cost REML` = iid_cost_reml, `iid cost NCV` = iid_cost_ncv) |>
  pretty()
save_tab(Q1, "synthetic-question1")
by_fam <- core_dep |>
  group_by(family, arm) |>
  summarise(lo = min(coverage_mean), hi = max(coverage_mean), .groups = "drop")
bf <- \(fam, a) c(by_fam$lo[by_fam$family == fam & by_fam$arm == a], by_fam$hi[by_fam$family == fam & by_fam$arm == a])
```

Model-based intervals undercover in every dependent cell and every family
(@fig-coverage-core): at G = 100, Gaussian `r rng(bf("gaussian", "reml_model"))`, Poisson
`r rng(bf("poisson", "reml_model"))`, binary `r rng(bf("binomial", "reml_model"))`. REML + CL2
covers `r rng(bf("gaussian", "reml_cl2"))`, `r rng(bf("poisson", "reml_cl2"))` and
`r rng(bf("binomial", "reml_cl2"))`. The signal level does not change this (REML + CL2's
core-factorial average per signal level is within
`r pp(max(abs(PROF$estimate[PROF$factor == "signal" & PROF$value == "coverage_reml_cl2"] - LEVEL)))`
of nominal; @tbl-core-coverage-all lists every cell). On the recommendation pool (dependent
core cells at G = 100 plus the Gaussian misregistration cell) the calibration error of the
model-based intervals is `r rng(Q1$estimate[Q1$name == "ce_reml_model"])`, that of
REML + CL2 `r rng(Q1$estimate[Q1$name == "ce_reml_cl2"])` (@tbl-q1). NCV + CL2 without the
bias allowance is less well calibrated (`r rng(Q1$estimate[Q1$name == "ce_ncv_cl2"])`;
binary responses worst). Under independent errors at G = 100, CL2 costs
`r rng_pp(Q1$estimate[Q1$name == "iid_cost_reml"])` of coverage relative to the model-based
intervals, which overcover there (`r rng(cov_of(core_iid, "reml_model"))`); at G = 40 the
cost is `r rng_pp(iid40_cost$cost)` (largest for the binary mean).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-q1
#| tbl-cap: "Question 1 on the recommendation pool: calibration error (CE) of model-based and CL2 intervals for the REML and the NCV fit, the paired gain of CL2, and the coverage lost by CL2 in the independent-error core cells at G = 100. Brackets: 95% replicate-bootstrap intervals."
show(q1)
```

### Lower tails of pointwise coverage

```{r fig-lower-tail}
#| fig-cap: "The 5% quantile over the evaluation grid of pointwise coverage (the worst 5% of grid points), core cells at the default signal level. Bars ± 2 MC SE."
#| fig-height: 5.5
d <- S |>
  filter(block == "core", signal == "mid", estimand %in% c("mean", "beta"), arm %in% MAIN_ARMS) |>
  mutate(arm = label_arm(arm), estimand = label_estimand(estimand), error = label_error(error), family = label_family(family), G = paste0("G = ", G))
fig <- coverage_plot(d, "error", vars(G, estimand), vars(family), x = "pointwise_q05", se = "pointwise_q05_se", xlab = "5% quantile of pointwise coverage")
save_fig(fig, "lower-tail-core", 6.5, 5.5)
fig
tail_tab <- S |>
  filter(block == "core", estimand %in% c("mean", "beta"), arm %in% MAIN_ARMS) |>
  group_by(dependence = if_else(error == "iid", "independent", "dependent"), G, estimand, arm) |>
  summarise(q05_min = min(pointwise_q05), q05_median = median(pointwise_q05), coverage_min = min(coverage_mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(arm = label_arm(arm), estimand = label_estimand(estimand))
save_tab(tail_tab, "synthetic-lower-tail-core")
tq <- \(a, e, g, dep = "dependent") tail_tab$q05_min[tail_tab$arm == ARM_LABELS[a] & tail_tab$estimand == ESTIMAND_LABELS[e] & tail_tab$G == g & tail_tab$dependence == dep]
```

Grid averages hide where an interval fails. The 5% quantile of pointwise coverage
(@fig-lower-tail; per-arm minima and medians in @tbl-lower-tail) is
`r rng(c(tq("reml_cl2", "beta", 100), tq("reml_cl2", "mean", 100)))` or higher for
REML + CL2 in the dependent cells at G = 100 (worst cell) and
`r rng(c(tq("reml_cl2", "beta", 40), tq("reml_cl2", "mean", 40)))` at G = 40; for the
model-based intervals it is as low as `r rng(c(tq("reml_model", "beta", 100), tq("reml_model", "mean", 100)))`.
NCV + CL2 without the allowance reaches `r f(tq("ncv_cl2", "beta", 40))` for β at G = 40
(binary responses). Under independent errors REML + CL2's lower tail for the mean is
`r f(tq("reml_cl2", "mean", 40, "independent"))` at G = 40.

### Studentised errors of the REML fit

```{r zstats-synthetic}
zs_avail <- !is.null(ZS)
# the mean's stored records hold link-scale estimates and SEs next to the response-scale
# truth, so z is defined for the mean only in Gaussian cells
zs_tab <- if (zs_avail) ZS |>
  filter(fit == "REML", !(estimand == "mean" & fit_family != "gaussian")) |>
  group_by(block, family, error, G, basis, covariate, estimand) |>
  summarise(across(c(z_mean_cl2, z_sd_cl2, share_big_cl2, z_mean_model, z_sd_model, share_big_model), mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(block, family, error, G, basis, estimand) else NULL
if (zs_avail) save_tab(zs_tab, "synthetic-zstats-reml")
zs_blocks <- if (zs_avail) sort(unique(ZS$block)) else character()
zs_dep <- if (zs_avail) zs_tab |> filter(error != "iid") else NULL
zs_iid <- if (zs_avail) zs_tab |> filter(error == "iid") else NULL
```

```{r zstats-synthetic-text}
zc <- if (zs_avail) zs_tab |> filter(block == "core") else NULL
zcv <- \(col, dep = TRUE, g = 100, e = "beta") zc[[col]][(zc$error != "iid") == dep & zc$G == g & zc$estimand == e]
zx <- if (zs_avail) zs_tab |> filter(block %in% c("warp", "rough_truth", "dense_grid", "oscillating", "families", "heteroskedastic", "lowrank_covariate", "term_type"), error != "iid") else NULL
zb <- if (zs_avail) zs_tab |> filter(block == "basis_size", error != "iid", estimand == "beta") else NULL
za <- if (zs_avail) ZS |> filter(fit == "REML", estimand == "alpha", error != "iid") else NULL
zav <- \(fam, blk = "core", g = 100, col = "z_mean_cl2", b = "default") za[[col]][za$family == fam & za$block == blk & za$G == g & za$basis == b]
zg <- if (zs_avail) ZS |> filter(fit == "REML", estimand == "gamma", error != "iid", block == "core") else NULL
```

`r if (zs_avail) sprintf("The studentised error z = (estimate − truth) / SE of the REML fit, pooled over grid points and replicates, is a descriptive diagnostic: an SD of z above 1 with a centred mean indicates SE underestimation, a shifted mean a bias, but the pooling over grid points cannot separate a global scale error from spatially varying bias (local biases of opposite sign cancel in the mean and inflate the SD), so the share of |z| > 1.96 is reported beside the SD (a normal pivot with that SD would give a predictable share). It is computed for β, α(t) and γ(t) in every cell (link scale) and for the mean in Gaussian cells (the stored mean records hold link-scale estimates next to response-scale truths). Means over cells (@tbl-zstats-synthetic; per-cell values in the CSV): in the dependent core cells at G = 100 the SD of z with the CL2 SE is %s for β and %s for the Gaussian mean (mean of z %s; %s%% of |z| > 1.96), against %s with the model-based SE; at G = 40 it is %s for β and %s for the mean, which matches the 1–2 pp coverage loss of REML + CL2 there. Under independent errors the CL2 SE is conservative for β (SD %s at G = 100), matching its coverage near 0.98. Across the dependent extension cells (misregistration, rough truth, dense grid, sign-changing, extended families, heteroskedastic, low-rank, smooth-effect) the SD of z for β is %s and the mean of z %s; with the largest bases the SD falls to %s. For β and the Gaussian mean, therefore, the studentised error is centred and its SD exceeds 1 by a few per cent wherever REML + CL2 falls short. The GLM intercept α(t) is different: its studentised error is shifted under dependence, mean of z %s for binary responses at G = 100 (%s at G = 40; dense grid %s; large and xlarge bases %s and %s) and %s for Poisson (independent errors: %s and %s), while Gaussian α(t) and every γ(t) stay within %s: a link-scale bias of the GLM intercept that grows with the basis size and is not corrected by CL2, which explains part of the binary α(t) shortfall.", rng(zcv("z_sd_cl2")), rng(zcv("z_sd_cl2", e = "mean")), rng(c(zcv("z_mean_cl2"), zcv("z_mean_cl2", e = "mean"))), rng(100 * c(zcv("share_big_cl2"), zcv("share_big_cl2", e = "mean")), 1), rng(c(zcv("z_sd_model"), zcv("z_sd_model", e = "mean"))), rng(zcv("z_sd_cl2", g = 40)), rng(zcv("z_sd_cl2", g = 40, e = "mean")), rng(zcv("z_sd_cl2", dep = FALSE)), rng(zx$z_sd_cl2[zx$estimand == "beta"]), rng(zx$z_mean_cl2[zx$estimand == "beta"]), f(min(zb$z_sd_cl2), 2), rng(zav("binomial")), rng(zav("binomial", g = 40)), rng(zav("binomial", "dense_grid")), rng(zav("binomial", "basis_size", b = "large")), rng(zav("binomial", "basis_size", b = "xlarge")), rng(zav("poisson")), rng(ZS$z_mean_cl2[ZS$fit == "REML" & ZS$estimand == "alpha" & ZS$error == "iid" & ZS$block == "core" & ZS$family == "binomial"]), rng(ZS$z_mean_cl2[ZS$fit == "REML" & ZS$estimand == "alpha" & ZS$error == "iid" & ZS$block == "core" & ZS$family == "poisson"]), rng(c(abs(zav("gaussian")), abs(zg$z_mean_cl2)))) else "The studentised-error diagnostics for the synthetic study are pending (LRZ task records)."`

### Grid density

```{r fig-grid}
#| fig-cap: "Coverage of β and the mean at D = 61 (core, default signal) and D = 241 (dense-grid block), G = 100. Bars ± 2 MC SE."
#| fig-height: 3.5
d <- S |>
  filter((block == "core" & G == 100 & signal == "mid") | block == "dense_grid", estimand %in% c("beta", "mean"), arm %in% c("reml_model", "reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2_bias")) |>
  mutate(arm = label_arm(arm), estimand = label_estimand(estimand), error = label_error_short(error), family = label_family(family), D = factor(D))
fig <- ggplot(d, aes(D, coverage_mean, colour = arm, group = arm)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = LEVEL, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = coverage_mean - 2 * coverage_se, ymax = coverage_mean + 2 * coverage_se), size = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(estimand ~ family + error) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ARM_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "grid points per curve D", y = "coverage") +
  theme_doc + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
save_fig(fig, "coverage-grid", 6.5, 3.5)
fig
grid_tab <- MC |>
  filter(block == "dense_grid", estimand == "beta", value %in% c("coverage_reml_model", "coverage_reml_cl2", "coverage_ncv_cl2", "coverage_ncv_cl2_bias", "log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml")) |>
  mutate(diff = ci(estimate, lower, upper)) |>
  select(family, error, value, diff) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = value, values_from = diff) |>
  rename(`model-based` = coverage_reml_model, `REML + CL2` = coverage_reml_cl2, `NCV + CL2` = coverage_ncv_cl2, `bias-aware` = coverage_ncv_cl2_bias, `log MSE ratio` = log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml) |>
  pretty()
save_tab(MC |> filter(block == "dense_grid"), "synthetic-grid-contrasts")
gd <- \(v, err = c("ou", "fpc")) dense$estimate[dense$value == v & dense$error %in% err]
```

Denser grids make model-based intervals worse, not better: from D = 61 to 241 their
coverage of β drops by `r rng_pp(-gd("coverage_reml_model"))` under dependence
(`r rng_pp(-gd("coverage_reml_model", "iid"))` under independent errors), while REML + CL2
changes by `r rng_pp(gd("coverage_reml_cl2"))` and the bias-aware NCV interval by
`r rng_pp(gd("coverage_ncv_cl2_bias"))` (@fig-grid, @tbl-grid). NCV's estimation advantage
grows with the grid: the log NCV/REML MSE ratio falls by `r rng(-gd("log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml"))`
under dependence, a factor of `r rng(exp(-gd("log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml")), 1)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grid
#| tbl-cap: "Dense grid (D = 241) minus the matching core cell (D = 61), β at G = 100: coverage differences and the difference of log(MSE NCV / MSE REML), 95% replicate-bootstrap intervals."
show(grid_tab)
```

### Number of curves

```{r g40}
g_tab <- S |>
  filter(block == "core", estimand %in% c("mean", "beta"), arm %in% c(MAIN_ARMS, "ncv_cl2f_bias")) |>
  select(family, error, signal, estimand, arm, G, coverage_mean) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = G, values_from = coverage_mean, names_prefix = "G") |>
  mutate(diff = G100 - G40)
g_sum <- g_tab |>
  group_by(dependence = if_else(error == "iid", "independent", "dependent"), family, estimand, arm) |>
  summarise(`G = 40` = mean(G40), `G = 100` = mean(G100), `loss at G = 40` = mean(diff), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(arm = label_arm(arm), estimand = label_estimand(estimand), family = label_family(family)) |>
  arrange(dependence, family, estimand, arm)
save_tab(g_sum, "synthetic-G40-vs-100")
gl <- \(a, dep = "dependent") g_sum$`loss at G = 40`[g_sum$arm == ARM_LABELS[a] & g_sum$dependence == dep]
g40_bin <- g_sum |> filter(dependence == "dependent", family == "binary")
g40_bin_ncv_beta <- g40_bin[["G = 40"]][g40_bin$arm == ARM_LABELS["ncv_cl2"] & g40_bin$estimand == ESTIMAND_LABELS["beta"]]
```

With 40 instead of 100 curves REML + CL2 loses `r rng_pp(gl("reml_cl2"))` of coverage in
the dependent cells (averaged over signal levels and error processes per family and
estimand; @tbl-g40), the bias-aware NCV interval `r rng_pp(gl("ncv_cl2_bias"))`. NCV + CL2
without the allowance loses `r rng_pp(gl("ncv_cl2"))`, most for binary responses, where it
covers β at `r f(g40_bin_ncv_beta)` at G = 40. The model-based intervals are already far
off at both G.

### Signal strength and truth roughness

```{r fig-signal-truth}
#| fig-cap: "Coverage of β by signal level and truth roughness (smooth = core cells, rough = rough-truth block), G = 100, smooth (DTI-FPC) and independent errors. Bars ± 2 MC SE."
#| fig-height: 5
d <- S |>
  filter(block %in% c("core", "rough_truth"), G == 100, error %in% c("iid", "fpc"), estimand == "beta", arm %in% c("reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2", "ncv_cl2_bias", "ncv_cl2f_bias")) |>
  mutate(arm = label_arm(arm), family = label_family(family), error = label_error(error), signal = label_signal(signal), truth = paste(if_else(truth == "wiggly", "rough", "smooth"), "truth"))
fig <- coverage_plot(d, "signal", vars(truth, error), vars(family))
save_fig(fig, "coverage-signal-truth", 6.5, 5)
fig
st <- S |> filter(block %in% c("core", "rough_truth"), G == 100, error %in% c("iid", "fpc"), estimand == "beta")
stv <- \(a, tr, err = "fpc") st$coverage_mean[st$arm == a & st$truth == tr & st$error == err]
st_tab <- cov_wide(st$cell, "beta", c("reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2", "ncv_cl2_bias", "ncv_cl2f_bias")) |> select(-D, -basis, -G) |> pretty()
save_tab(st_tab, "synthetic-signal-truth-beta")
```

Signal strength changes little; truth roughness does (@fig-signal-truth, @tbl-signal-truth).
With the rough truth and dependent errors NCV + CL2 covers β at `r rng(stv("ncv_cl2", "wiggly"))`
(smooth truth: `r rng(stv("ncv_cl2", "smooth"))`), because NCV's extra smoothing now buys
bias; the bias allowance restores `r rng(stv("ncv_cl2_bias", "wiggly"))`, still short of
REML + CL2's `r rng(stv("reml_cl2", "wiggly"))`. With the smooth truth the allowance
overcovers β (`r rng(stv("ncv_cl2_bias", "smooth"))`). The frequentist-CL2 variant of the
allowance undercovers under independent errors with a rough truth
(`r rng(stv("ncv_cl2f_bias", "wiggly", "iid"))`).

### Estimands and term types

```{r estimands}
est_tab <- S |>
  filter(block == "core", G == 100, signal == "mid", arm %in% MAIN_ARMS) |>
  group_by(dependence = if_else(error == "iid", "independent", "dependent"), family, estimand, arm) |>
  summarise(coverage = mean(coverage_mean), q05 = mean(pointwise_q05), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(arm = label_arm(arm), estimand = label_estimand(estimand), family = label_family(family))
est_wide <- est_tab |>
  select(-q05) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = coverage) |>
  arrange(dependence, family, estimand)
save_tab(est_tab, "synthetic-coverage-by-estimand")
ev <- \(a, e, dep = "dependent") est_tab$coverage[est_tab$arm == ARM_LABELS[a] & est_tab$estimand == ESTIMAND_LABELS[e] & est_tab$dependence == dep]
m2 <- MC |> filter(block == "term_type", estimand == "main")
m2_tab <- m2 |>
  filter(value %in% c("coverage_reml_model", "coverage_reml_cl2", "coverage_ncv_cl2_bias", "log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml")) |>
  mutate(diff = ci(estimate, lower, upper)) |>
  select(family, error, value, diff) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = value, values_from = diff) |>
  rename(`model-based` = coverage_reml_model, `REML + CL2` = coverage_reml_cl2, `bias-aware` = coverage_ncv_cl2_bias, `log MSE ratio` = log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml) |>
  pretty()
save_tab(MC |> filter(block == "term_type"), "synthetic-term-type-contrasts")
m2v <- \(v, err = c("ou", "fpc")) m2$estimate[m2$value == v & m2$error %in% err]
```

The pattern is the same for all four estimands (@tbl-estimands): in the dependent cells at
G = 100 and default signal the model-based intervals cover α(t) at
`r rng(ev("reml_model", "alpha"))`, γ(t) at `r rng(ev("reml_model", "gamma"))`, β at
`r rng(ev("reml_model", "beta"))` and the mean at `r rng(ev("reml_model", "mean"))`;
REML + CL2 covers them at `r rng(c(ev("reml_cl2", "alpha"), ev("reml_cl2", "gamma"), ev("reml_cl2", "beta"), ev("reml_cl2", "mean")))`
(the low end is binary α(t)/γ(t)). Replacing the functional covariate by a smooth effect
f(x,t) of a scalar covariate changes REML + CL2's coverage by `r rng_pp(m2v("coverage_reml_cl2"))`
under dependence (paired difference to the matching ff cell, @tbl-term-type); NCV's
relative advantage for the surface is smaller in that model (the log MSE ratio is higher
by `r rng(m2v("log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml"))`, i.e. the ratio is `r rng(exp(m2v("log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml")), 1)`
times larger), but still below one.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-estimands
#| tbl-cap: "Coverage by estimand (mean over error processes within dependence class), core cells, G = 100, default signal."
show(est_wide)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-term-type
#| tbl-cap: "Smooth-effect model f(x,t) minus the matching ff(X) cell (surface estimand; G = 100, default signal): coverage differences and the difference in log(MSE NCV / MSE REML); 95% replicate-bootstrap intervals."
show(m2_tab)
```

### Heteroskedasticity, misregistration and sign-changing correlation

```{r extensions}
het_tab <- cov_wide(DESIGN$cell[DESIGN$block == "heteroskedastic" | (DESIGN$block == "core" & DESIGN$error == "fpc" & DESIGN$family == "gaussian" & DESIGN$signal == "mid")], c("mean", "beta", "gamma"), c(MAIN_ARMS, "ar1_model")) |>
  select(-D, -basis, -signal, -truth, -family)
hv <- \(a, e, err) het_tab[[a]][het_tab$estimand == e & het_tab$error %in% err]
het_show <- pretty(het_tab)
save_tab(het_show, "synthetic-heteroskedastic-coverage")
# misregistration: the AR(1)-on-warp cell (same DGP as the Gaussian rough-truth warp cell at G = 100) supplies the AR(1) column of that row
warp_raw <- cov_wide(DESIGN$cell[DESIGN$block %in% c("warp", "warp_ar1")], c("mean", "beta"), c(MAIN_ARMS, "ncv_cl2f_bias", "ar1_model"))
warp_tab <- warp_raw |>
  group_by(family, G, signal, truth, estimand) |>
  summarise(across(c(all_of(MAIN_ARMS), ncv_cl2f_bias, ar1_model), \(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")
wv <- \(a, fam, e = "mean") warp_tab[[a]][warp_tab$family == fam & warp_tab$estimand == e]
warp_show <- pretty(warp_tab)
save_tab(warp_show, "synthetic-misregistration-coverage")
osc_tab <- cov_wide(DESIGN$cell[DESIGN$block == "oscillating"], c("mean", "beta"), c(MAIN_ARMS, "ar1_model")) |>
  select(-D, -basis, -signal, -truth, -G)
osc_show <- pretty(osc_tab)
save_tab(osc_show, "synthetic-oscillating-coverage")
```

A variance profile along t leaves every recipe where it was (@tbl-het). Variance that
depends on the scalar covariate breaks the model-based intervals for γ(t)
(`r rng(hv("reml_model", "gamma", c("fpc_het", "fpc_raw_het")))`) and the AR(1) model's
(`r rng(na.omit(hv("ar1_model", "gamma", c("fpc_het", "fpc_raw_het"))))`), while REML + CL2
covers γ at `r rng(hv("reml_cl2", "gamma", c("fpc_het", "fpc_raw_het")))`.

Misregistration (each curve observed on its own clock, the estimand being the observed-clock
mean and its smeared coefficients) gives model-based coverage of
`r rng(wv("reml_model", "gaussian"))` for the Gaussian mean and REML + CL2 coverage of
`r rng(wv("reml_cl2", "gaussian"))` (@tbl-warp). For misregistered Poisson data every
recipe undercovers the mean (REML + CL2 `r rng(wv("reml_cl2", "poisson"))`, bias-aware NCV
`r rng(wv("ncv_cl2_bias", "poisson"))`); binary responses are unaffected
(`r rng(wv("reml_cl2", "binomial"))`). Sign-changing correlations behave like the other
dependent processes: model-based `r rng(c(osc_tab$reml_model))`, REML + CL2
`r rng(c(osc_tab$reml_cl2))` (@tbl-osc).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-warp
#| tbl-cap: "Misregistration cells (high signal): coverage of the observed-clock estimands. GLM cells score the mean only; the AR(1) column comes from the Gaussian cells that ran the AR(1) arm."
show(warp_show)
```

### Extended families

```{r families}
fam_cov <- cov_wide(DESIGN$cell[DESIGN$block == "families"], c("mean", "beta"), MAIN_ARMS) |>
  left_join(distinct(DESIGN, cell, fit_family), by = "cell") |>
  select(family, fit_family, error, estimand, all_of(MAIN_ARMS))
fam_mse <- MSE_RATIO |>
  filter(block == "families", estimand %in% c("mean", "beta")) |>
  mutate(`MSE ratio NCV/REML` = ci(ratio, ratio_lower, ratio_upper, 2)) |>
  select(family, fit_family, error, estimand, `MSE ratio NCV/REML`)
fam_tab <- left_join(fam_cov, fam_mse, by = c("family", "fit_family", "error", "estimand"))
fv <- \(a, err = "fpc") fam_tab[[a]][fam_tab$error == err & fam_tab$family == fam_tab$fit_family]
fam_show <- pretty(fam_tab)
save_tab(fam_show, "synthetic-extended-families")
```

Scaled-t, beta and negative-binomial responses repeat the pattern (@tbl-families): under
the smooth error process model-based coverage is `r rng(fv("reml_model"))` and REML + CL2's
`r rng(fv("reml_cl2"))`; the NCV/REML MSE ratio for β is
`r rng(MSE_RATIO$ratio[MSE_RATIO$block == "families" & MSE_RATIO$error == "fpc" & MSE_RATIO$estimand == "beta" & MSE_RATIO$fit_family == MSE_RATIO$family])`.
Fitting negative-binomial data as Poisson costs the model-based intervals most
(`r rng(fam_tab$reml_model[fam_tab$fit_family == "poisson" & fam_tab$family == "nb"])`),
REML + CL2 little (`r rng(fam_tab$reml_cl2[fam_tab$fit_family == "poisson" & fam_tab$family == "nb"])`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-families
#| tbl-cap: "Extended families at G = 100: coverage per arm and the NCV/REML MSE ratio (95% bootstrap interval)."
show(fam_show)
```

### Basis size

```{r fig-basis}
#| fig-cap: "Basis size (nested bases; large and xlarge halve and quarter the knot spacing), G = 100, default signal, smooth truth. Left: EDF of the ff term under REML and NCV. Middle: NCV/REML MSE ratio for β and the mean with bootstrap intervals. Right: coverage of β."
#| fig-height: 4.5
basis_levels <- c("default", "large", "xlarge")
bcells <- DESIGN |>
  filter(block == "basis_size" | (block == "core" & G == 100 & signal == "mid" & error %in% c("iid", "fpc") & family %in% c("gaussian", "poisson", "binomial")))
edf_b <- EDF |>
  filter(cell %in% bcells$cell, term == "te(X.smat,X.tmat):L.X", fit %in% c("REML", "NCV")) |>
  mutate(basis = factor(basis, basis_levels), family = label_family(family), error = label_error(error))
p1 <- ggplot(edf_b, aes(basis, edf_mean, colour = fit, group = fit)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  facet_grid(error ~ family) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(REML = "#0072B2", NCV = "#D55E00"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "EDF of the ff term") + theme_doc
mse_b <- MSE_RATIO |>
  filter(cell %in% bcells$cell, estimand %in% c("beta", "mean")) |>
  mutate(basis = factor(basis, basis_levels), family = label_family(family), error = label_error(error), estimand = label_estimand(estimand))
p2 <- ggplot(mse_b, aes(basis, ratio, colour = estimand, group = estimand)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = ratio_lower, ymax = ratio_upper), size = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(error ~ family) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#000000", "#56B4E9"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "MSE NCV / MSE REML") + theme_doc
cov_b <- S |>
  filter(cell %in% bcells$cell, estimand == "beta", arm %in% MAIN_ARMS) |>
  mutate(basis = factor(basis, basis_levels), family = label_family(family), error = label_error(error), arm = label_arm(arm))
p3 <- ggplot(cov_b, aes(basis, coverage_mean, colour = arm, group = arm)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = LEVEL, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = coverage_mean - 2 * coverage_se, ymax = coverage_mean + 2 * coverage_se), size = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(error ~ family) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ARM_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "coverage of beta") + theme_doc
fig <- (p1 | p2 | p3) & theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1), strip.text = element_text(size = 6))
save_fig(fig, "basis-size", 9, 4.5)
fig
basis_tab <- cov_b |>
  select(family, error, basis, arm, coverage_mean, score_mean, width_mean) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(coverage_mean, score_mean, width_mean)) |>
  left_join(mse_b |> filter(estimand == ESTIMAND_LABELS["beta"]) |> select(family, error, basis, mse_ratio_beta = ratio), by = c("family", "error", "basis")) |>
  arrange(family, error, basis)
names(basis_tab) <- sub("coverage_mean_", "cov: ", sub("score_mean_", "IS: ", sub("width_mean_", "width: ", names(basis_tab))))
save_tab(basis_tab, "synthetic-basis-size")
ed <- \(fit, b, err = "fpc") edf_b$edf_mean[edf_b$fit == fit & edf_b$basis == b & edf_b$error == ERROR_LABELS[err]]
bs <- \(a, b, err = "fpc") cov_b$coverage_mean[cov_b$arm == ARM_LABELS[a] & cov_b$basis == b & cov_b$error == ERROR_LABELS[err]]
bis <- MC |> filter(block == "basis_size", estimand == "beta", value == "log_score_ratio_proposal_fallback")
wr_b <- width_ratio |> filter(cell %in% bcells$cell, estimand == "beta", error == "fpc")
```

As the bases grow, REML's ff EDF under the smooth error process rises from
`r rng(ed("REML", "default"), 0)` (default) to `r rng(ed("REML", "large"), 0)` (large) and
`r rng(ed("REML", "xlarge"), 0)` (xlarge) across the three families, while NCV's rises from
`r rng(ed("NCV", "default"), 0)` to `r rng(ed("NCV", "large"), 0)` and `r rng(ed("NCV", "xlarge"), 0)`:
REML absorbs the dependence into the surface. The NCV/REML MSE ratio for β falls to
`r rng(mse_b$ratio[mse_b$basis == "xlarge" & mse_b$error == ERROR_LABELS["fpc"] & mse_b$estimand == ESTIMAND_LABELS["beta"]])`
with the xlarge basis (@fig-basis, @tbl-basis). REML + CL2 stays calibrated
(β `r rng(bs("reml_cl2", "xlarge"))` at xlarge), whereas the bias-aware NCV interval
overcovers more with every step (`r rng(bs("ncv_cl2_bias", "default"))` → `r rng(bs("ncv_cl2_bias", "large"))`
→ `r rng(bs("ncv_cl2_bias", "xlarge"))`) because the allowance is the difference of two
estimates and inherits REML's growing noise; its width relative to REML + CL2 is
`r rng(wr_b$bias_aware[wr_b$basis == "default"], 2)` (default) and `r rng(wr_b$bias_aware[wr_b$basis == "xlarge"], 2)`
(xlarge), and its interval score still beats REML + CL2's (log score ratio
`r rng(bis$estimate[bis$error == "fpc"])` under the smooth process) because REML + CL2's
intervals widen with REML's variance. Under independent errors every arm overcovers β with
the larger bases (`r rng(bs("reml_cl2", "xlarge", "iid"))`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-basis
#| tbl-cap: "Basis size: coverage (cov), interval score (IS) and mean width of β intervals per arm, and the NCV/REML MSE ratio for β."
show(pretty(basis_tab), digits = 2)
```

## Estimation

### NCV versus REML by factor and estimand

```{r fig-mse}
#| fig-cap: "MSE of the NCV fit relative to the REML fit (log scale) with 95% replicate-bootstrap intervals, G = 100, by error process, family and signal level, for the smooth truth (core), the rough truth, the smooth-effect model and the low-rank covariate. The surface column shows β(s,t) for the ff model and f(x,t) for the smooth-effect model."
#| fig-height: 6
d <- MSE_RATIO |>
  filter(block %in% c("core", "rough_truth", "term_type", "lowrank_covariate"), G == 100, estimand %in% c("beta", "f", "mean", "gamma")) |>
  mutate(
    estimand = factor(recode(estimand, mean = "E(Y | X)", beta = "surface: beta(s,t) or f(x,t)", f = "surface: beta(s,t) or f(x,t)", gamma = "gamma(t)"), c("E(Y | X)", "surface: beta(s,t) or f(x,t)", "gamma(t)")),
    setting = factor(recode(block, core = "smooth truth", rough_truth = "rough truth", term_type = "f(x,t) model", lowrank_covariate = "low-rank X"), c("smooth truth", "rough truth", "f(x,t) model", "low-rank X")),
    error = label_error(error), signal = label_signal(signal), family = label_family(family)
  )
fig <- ggplot(d, aes(ratio, error, colour = family, shape = signal)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = ratio_lower, xmax = ratio_upper), position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), size = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(setting ~ estimand, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(low = 1, mid = 16, high = 17), name = "signal") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Gaussian = "#000000", Poisson = "#56B4E9", binary = "#CC79A7"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "MSE of NCV / MSE of REML (log scale; G = 100)", y = NULL) +
  theme_doc
save_fig(fig, "mse-ratio", 6.5, 6)
fig
prof_err <- PROF |>
  filter(value == "log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml", factor == "error") |>
  mutate(ratio = ci(exp(estimate), exp(lower), exp(upper), 2)) |>
  select(family, estimand, error = name, ratio) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = error, values_from = ratio) |>
  pretty()
save_tab(prof_err, "synthetic-mse-ratio-by-error")
prof_G <- PROF |>
  filter(value == "log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml", factor == "G") |>
  mutate(ratio = exp(estimate)) |>
  select(family, estimand, G = name, ratio) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = G, values_from = ratio, names_prefix = "G")
pe <- \(e, err) exp(PROF$estimate[PROF$value == "log_mse_ratio_ncv_reml" & PROF$factor == "error" & PROF$name %in% err & PROF$estimand == e])
rough <- MSE_RATIO |> filter(block == "rough_truth", error == "fpc")
lowr <- MSE_RATIO |> filter(block == "lowrank_covariate")
```

NCV's gain is a dependence effect concentrated on the bivariate surface (@fig-mse,
@tbl-mse-error). Averaged over the whole core factorial (both G, all signal levels), the
NCV/REML MSE ratio for β is `r rng(pe("beta", c("ou", "fpc")))` under dependent errors and
`r rng(pe("beta", "iid"))` under independent errors; for the mean `r rng(pe("mean", c("ou", "fpc")))`
and `r rng(pe("mean", "iid"))`. In the dependent cells at G = 100 (the pool of the summary)
the ratios are `r rng(ratio_of(r_dep, "beta"))` for β, `r rng(ratio_of(r_dep, "mean"))` for the
mean, `r rng(ratio_of(r_dep, "gamma"))` for γ(t) and `r rng(ratio_of(r_dep, "alpha"))` for
α(t). With the rough truth the gain for β shrinks to `r rng(rough$ratio[rough$estimand == "beta"])`
(smooth process), the mean's to `r rng(rough$ratio[rough$estimand == "mean"])`. A low-rank
covariate (spectrum like the running data's knee angle) makes the β gain larger under
dependence (`r rng(lowr$ratio[lowr$estimand == "beta" & lowr$error == "fpc"])`) and removes it
under independent errors (`r rng(lowr$ratio[lowr$estimand == "beta" & lowr$error == "iid"])`).
The ratio is nearly the same at G = 40 and G = 100 (β: `r rng(prof_G$G40[prof_G$estimand == "beta"])`
vs `r rng(prof_G$G100[prof_G$estimand == "beta"])`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mse-error
#| tbl-cap: "NCV/REML MSE ratio: geometric mean over the core cells of each error process (all G and signal levels), 95% replicate-bootstrap intervals."
show(prof_err)
```

### Bias and variance

```{r fig-bias-variance}
#| fig-cap: "Share of squared bias and variance in the integrated squared error of β and the mean for the REML and NCV fits, core cells at G = 100 and default signal, smooth truth and (where run) rough truth. Absolute values are in the supplementary table."
#| fig-height: 4.5
bv <- S |>
  filter((block == "core" | block == "rough_truth") & G == 100 & signal == "mid", estimand %in% c("beta", "mean"), arm %in% c("reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2")) |>
  transmute(family = label_family(family), error = label_error_short(error), truth = if_else(truth == "wiggly", "rough", "smooth"), estimand = label_estimand(estimand), fit = if_else(arm == "reml_cl2", "REML", "NCV"), `squared bias` = bias2, variance = variance) |>
  mutate(x = factor(paste(fit, truth), c("REML smooth", "NCV smooth", "REML rough", "NCV rough"))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`squared bias`, variance), names_to = "component", values_to = "value")
fig <- ggplot(bv, aes(x, value, fill = component)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  facet_grid(estimand ~ family + error) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`squared bias` = "#D55E00", variance = "#0072B2"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "fit and truth", y = "share of the integrated squared error") +
  theme_doc + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 6), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, size = 6))
save_fig(fig, "bias-variance", 7.5, 4.5)
fig
bv_tab <- S |>
  filter(block %in% c("core", "rough_truth"), estimand %in% c("beta", "mean"), arm %in% c("reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2")) |>
  transmute(family, error, G, signal, truth, estimand, fit = if_else(arm == "reml_cl2", "REML", "NCV"), mse, mse_se, bias2, bias2_se, variance, bias_share = pmax(bias2, 0) / mse) |>
  arrange(family, error, G, signal, truth, estimand, fit)
save_tab(bv_tab, "synthetic-bias-variance")
bshare <- \(fit_sel, tr, e = "beta", err = c("ou", "fpc")) bv_tab$bias_share[bv_tab$fit == fit_sel & bv_tab$truth == tr & bv_tab$estimand == e & bv_tab$error %in% err & bv_tab$G == 100]
```

REML's excess error under dependence is variance, not bias: in the dependent core cells at
G = 100 the squared-bias share of REML's β error is `r rng(bshare("REML", "smooth"))`, of
NCV's `r rng(bshare("NCV", "smooth"))` (@fig-bias-variance). With the rough truth NCV's
bias share for β rises to `r rng(bshare("NCV", "wiggly", err = "fpc"))` (REML
`r rng(bshare("REML", "wiggly", err = "fpc"))`), the mechanism behind NCV + CL2's
undercoverage there. Per-cell values with the MC SEs of the MSE and of the squared-bias
estimate are in `synthetic-bias-variance.csv`.

### Effective degrees of freedom

```{r edf}
edf_core <- EDF |>
  filter(block == "core", G == 100, signal == "mid", fit %in% c("REML", "NCV")) |>
  mutate(term = recode(term, `s(yindex.vec)` = "alpha(t)", `te(X.smat,X.tmat):L.X` = "beta(s,t)", `s(yindex.vec):z` = "gamma(t)")) |>
  select(family, error, term, fit, edf_mean) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = fit, values_from = edf_mean) |>
  mutate(ratio = REML / NCV) |>
  arrange(term, family, error)
save_tab(EDF |> select(cell, block, family, error, G, signal, truth, basis, fit, term, edf_mean, edf_se, mean_log_sp), "synthetic-term-edf")
er <- \(term_sel, err) edf_core$ratio[edf_core$term == term_sel & edf_core$error %in% err]
```

Under dependent errors REML's ff EDF exceeds NCV's by a factor of
`r rng(er("beta(s,t)", c("ou", "fpc")))` (independent errors: `r rng(er("beta(s,t)", "iid"))`);
for α(t) the factor is `r rng(er("alpha(t)", c("ou", "fpc")))` and for γ(t)
`r rng(er("gamma(t)", c("ou", "fpc")))` (@tbl-edf). NCV's gain is largest where the EDF gap
is largest.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-edf
#| tbl-cap: "Mean EDF per term under REML and NCV, core cells at G = 100 and default signal."
show(pretty(edf_core))
```

### Pointwise NCV and the low-rank covariate

```{r pointwise}
pw <- W |>
  filter(contrast == "pointwise ncv vs reml: squared error", estimand %in% c("beta", "mean")) |>
  transmute(error, estimand, `MSE pointwise NCV / REML` = ci(ratio, ratio_lower, ratio_upper, 2)) |>
  pretty()
save_tab(pw, "synthetic-pointwise-ncv")
pwv <- \(e, err) W$ratio[W$contrast == "pointwise ncv vs reml: squared error" & W$estimand == e & W$error %in% err]
lowrank_tab <- MSE_RATIO |>
  filter(block == "lowrank_covariate" | (block == "core" & G == 100 & signal == "mid" & error %in% c("iid", "fpc") & family %in% c("gaussian", "poisson", "binomial"))) |>
  mutate(covariate = if_else(block == "core", "rich", "low-rank"), ratio_ci = ci(ratio, ratio_lower, ratio_upper, 2)) |>
  select(family, error, estimand, covariate, ratio_ci) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = covariate, values_from = ratio_ci) |>
  arrange(family, error, estimand) |>
  pretty()
save_tab(lowrank_tab, "synthetic-lowrank-mse")
```

Ordinary pointwise NCV (mgcv's default neighbourhoods) is no substitute for curve blocks:
under the smooth and the sign-changing error processes its β MSE is
`r rng(pwv("beta", c("fpc", "osc")))` times REML's and its mean MSE
`r rng(pwv("mean", c("fpc", "osc")))` times (@tbl-pointwise), because a held-out point
is predicted by its correlated neighbours.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pointwise
#| tbl-cap: "Pointwise (non-blocked) NCV relative to REML, Gaussian G = 100."
show(pw)
```

## The recommendation rule under both criteria {#sec-rule}

```{r rule}
rv_syn <- RV |>
  filter(data == "synthetic") |>
  select(family = group, estimand, criterion, ce_proposal, ce_fallback, score_ratio, decision) |>
  arrange(family, estimand, criterion) |>
  pretty()
save_tab(rv_syn, "synthetic-rule-variants")
save_tab(REC, "synthetic-recommendation")
save_tab(RECSIG, "synthetic-recommendation-by-signal")
rsym <- rv_syn |> filter(criterion == "symmetric")
runder <- rv_syn |> filter(criterion == "under only")
```

The recommendation rule compares the proposal (NCV + bias-aware CL2) with the fallback
(REML + CL2) on the pool per family and primary estimand: a recipe is adequate if its CE is
≤ 2 pp, and among adequate recipes the interval-score ratio decides (≤ 0.95 proposal,
≥ 1/0.95 fallback, otherwise the simpler fallback). Two calibration criteria are reported
(@tbl-rule): a symmetric one that counts over- and undercoverage alike, and one that counts
undercoverage only, since width is already priced by the interval score. Under the symmetric criterion the proposal fails
adequacy for β in every family (CE `r rng(rsym$ce_proposal[rsym$estimand == ESTIMAND_LABELS["beta"]])`,
from overcoverage near 0.98) and the rule picks the fallback for β and the proposal for
the mean; under the undercoverage-only criterion the proposal's CE is
`r rng(runder$ce_proposal)` and it is chosen for both estimands in all three families on
interval score (β ratio `r rng(runder$score_ratio[runder$estimand == ESTIMAND_LABELS["beta"]])`,
mean `r rng(runder$score_ratio[runder$estimand == ESTIMAND_LABELS["mean"]])`), at every
signal level (`synthetic-recommendation-by-signal.csv`).

**The rule's synthetic output is not the recommendation.** On the nine plasmode datasets the
undercoverage-only criterion does not select the proposal (@sec-plasmode-rule: no consistent
class, and the proposal undercovers β under REML-fitted truths), and the proposal's
interval-score advantage comes from a construction whose calibration depends on the truth's
smoothness (@sec-bias-aware).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rule
#| tbl-cap: "The recommendation rule on the synthetic pool under the symmetric and the undercoverage-only calibration criterion. CE = calibration error; score ratio = geometric mean of interval-score ratios proposal / fallback."
show(rv_syn)
```

## Bias-aware intervals: two failure mechanisms {#sec-bias-aware}

```{r bias-aware}
mc_rough <- HMC_S |> filter(truth == "wiggly")
mcv <- \(d, m, col) d[[col]][d$method == m]
fbias <- S |> filter(block %in% c("core", "rough_truth"), G == 100, estimand == "beta", arm == "ncv_cl2f_bias")
# hybrid in the synthetic study: dependent core cells at G = 100 (from the per-cell hybrid summary)
hs_cells <- HSUM_S |>
  filter(block == "core", G == 100, error != "iid", estimand %in% c("beta", "mean"), arm %in% c("reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2_bias", "hybrid")) |>
  select(cell, family, error, signal, estimand, arm, coverage_mean, pointwise_q05, width_mean, score_mean)
hs_wide <- hs_cells |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(coverage_mean, pointwise_q05, width_mean, score_mean))
hsv <- \(a, col, e = "beta") hs_wide[[paste0(col, "_", a)]][hs_wide$estimand == e]
hs_rough <- HSUM_S |>
  filter(block == "rough_truth", error == "fpc", estimand == "beta", arm %in% c("reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2_bias", "hybrid")) |>
  select(cell, arm, coverage_mean, pointwise_q05, width_mean, score_mean) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(coverage_mean, pointwise_q05, width_mean, score_mean))
hyb_tab <- bind_rows(
  hs_wide |> mutate(setting = "dependent core, G = 100"),
  HSUM_S |> filter(block == "rough_truth", error == "fpc", estimand %in% c("beta", "mean"), arm %in% c("reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2_bias", "hybrid")) |>
    select(cell, family, error, signal, estimand, arm, coverage_mean, pointwise_q05, width_mean, score_mean) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(coverage_mean, pointwise_q05, width_mean, score_mean)) |>
    mutate(setting = "rough truth, smooth errors")
) |>
  group_by(setting, estimand) |>
  summarise(
    n_cells = n(),
    `cov REML+CL2` = mean(coverage_mean_reml_cl2), `cov bias-aware` = mean(coverage_mean_ncv_cl2_bias), `cov hybrid` = mean(coverage_mean_hybrid),
    `q05 REML+CL2` = mean(pointwise_q05_reml_cl2), `q05 bias-aware` = mean(pointwise_q05_ncv_cl2_bias), `q05 hybrid` = mean(pointwise_q05_hybrid),
    `width bias-aware/REML+CL2` = exp(mean(log(width_mean_ncv_cl2_bias / width_mean_reml_cl2))),
    `width hybrid/REML+CL2` = exp(mean(log(width_mean_hybrid / width_mean_reml_cl2))),
    `IS bias-aware/REML+CL2` = exp(mean(log(score_mean_ncv_cl2_bias / score_mean_reml_cl2))),
    `IS hybrid/REML+CL2` = exp(mean(log(score_mean_hybrid / score_mean_reml_cl2))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(estimand = ESTIMAND_LABELS[estimand])
save_tab(hyb_tab, "synthetic-hybrid-bias-aware")
ht <- \(col, setting_sel = "dependent core, G = 100", e = "beta(s,t)") hyb_tab[[col]][hyb_tab$setting == setting_sel & hyb_tab$estimand == e]
```

The allowance δ = L(β̂_NCV − β̂_REML), added in quadrature to the CL2 standard error of the
NCV fit, fails in two ways.

*Inflation by REML's noise.* δ is a difference of two estimates and carries the sampling
variance of the REML fit, which the interval ignores. Where REML is noisy the interval is
too wide: in the dependent core cells at G = 100 the bias-aware β interval covers
`r f(ht("cov bias-aware"))` against REML + CL2's `r f(ht("cov REML+CL2"))` at
`r f(ht("width bias-aware/REML+CL2"), 2)` times the width (interval score ratio
`r f(ht("IS bias-aware/REML+CL2"), 2)`); with the larger bases the coverage reaches
`r rng(bs("ncv_cl2_bias", "xlarge"), 3)` (@tbl-hybrid-synth).

*Blindness to bias shared by both fits.* δ measures only how far NCV moved away from REML.
Where the truth is rougher than both fits, both are biased in the same direction and δ is
small. In the rough-truth cells with the smooth error process NCV + CL2 covers β at
`r rng(mcv(mc_rough, "ncv_cl2", "coverage_mean"))` with `r rng(100 * mcv(mc_rough, "ncv_cl2", "share_below_90"), 0)`%
of grid points below 0.90; the allowance lifts the average to `r rng(mcv(mc_rough, "ncv_cl2_bias", "coverage_mean"))`
but leaves `r rng(100 * mcv(mc_rough, "ncv_cl2_bias", "share_below_90"), 0)`% of points below 0.90,
and the remaining shortfall follows the truth's curvature (Spearman correlation of the
pointwise shortfall with |∂²β/∂s²| + |∂²β/∂t²|: `r rng(mcv(mc_rough, "ncv_cl2_bias", "cor_curv_spearman"))`,
against `r rng(mcv(mc_rough, "reml_cl2", "cor_curv_spearman"))` for REML + CL2;
@fig-maps-synthetic). The bias-aware interval's rough-truth lower tail
(`r f(ht("q05 bias-aware", "rough truth, smooth errors"))`) is no better than NCV + CL2's
smooth-truth tail (`r f(mean(S$pointwise_q05[S$block == "core" & S$G == 100 & S$error != "iid" & S$estimand == "beta" & S$arm == "ncv_cl2"]), 2)`).
The frequentist-CL2 variant is worse wherever the Bayesian one is
short (rough truth, β: `r rng(fbias$coverage_mean[fbias$truth == "wiggly"])`).

*The hybrid.* The NCV estimate with the REML fit's CL2 standard error covers β at
`r f(ht("cov hybrid"))` in the dependent core cells (5% quantile `r f(ht("q05 hybrid"))`,
width `r f(ht("width hybrid/REML+CL2"), 2)` and interval score `r f(ht("IS hybrid/REML+CL2"), 2)`
times REML + CL2's) and at `r f(ht("cov hybrid", "rough truth, smooth errors"))` with the
rough truth (5% quantile `r f(ht("q05 hybrid", "rough truth, smooth errors"))` against
REML + CL2's `r f(ht("q05 REML+CL2", "rough truth, smooth errors"))`). Its real-data results
are in @sec-hybrid.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-hybrid-synth
#| tbl-cap: "Bias-aware NCV interval and the hybrid (NCV estimate with REML's CL2 SE) next to REML + CL2: coverage (cov), 5% pointwise quantile (q05), and width and interval score (IS) relative to REML + CL2 (geometric means of per-cell ratios); dependent core cells at G = 100 and the rough-truth cells with the smooth error process."
show(hyb_tab, digits = 3)
```

```{r fig-maps-synthetic}
#| fig-cap: "Pointwise coverage of β(s,t) over the evaluation grid for four interval constructions, Gaussian, default signal, G = 100, smooth error process: smooth truth (top) and rough truth (bottom); the white contour marks 0.90. Right column: the truth's curvature |∂²β/∂s²| + |∂²β/∂t²|."
#| fig-height: 4.2
maps_s <- read_maps("synthetic")
map_cells <- maps_s |> filter(family == "gaussian", signal == "mid", error == "fpc", basis == "default") |> distinct(cell, truth)
mp <- maps_s |>
  filter(cell %in% map_cells$cell) |>
  mutate(method = label_arm(method), truth = paste(if_else(truth == "wiggly", "rough", "smooth"), "truth"))
curv <- mp |> filter(method == ARM_LABELS["reml_cl2"]) |> mutate(method = "curvature of truth")
p_cov <- ggplot(mp, aes(s, t)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = coverage)) +
  geom_contour(aes(z = coverage), breaks = 0.9, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(truth ~ method) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), name = "coverage") +
  coord_equal() + theme_doc + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 6))
p_curv <- ggplot(curv, aes(s, t, fill = curvature)) +
  geom_raster() +
  facet_grid(truth ~ method) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", name = "curvature") +
  coord_equal() + theme_doc + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 6), axis.title.y = element_blank())
fig <- p_cov + p_curv + plot_layout(widths = c(4, 1.15))
save_fig(fig, "coverage-maps-synthetic", 8, 4.2)
fig
```

## The AR(1) working model {#sec-ar1-fit}

*Fit.* The AR(1) working model is `pffr(algorithm = "bam", method = "fREML", rho = rho)`: mgcv's `bam()` with AR(1)
errors that restart at the first grid point of every curve, so curves stay independent and each curve's errors are
whitened with the same ρ. ρ is profiled. The model is fitted at every ρ in
{`r paste(CONST$AR_RHO_GRID, collapse = ", ")`}; the criterion is bam's fREML score, which already contains the
whitening log-determinant $-(n - G)\log(1/\sqrt{1 - \rho^2})$ (n data points, G curves), i.e. the restricted likelihood of the
AR(1) model. The minimising grid value is refined by a one-dimensional search (`optimize()`) between its two
neighbouring grid values, and the refined ρ replaces it if its criterion is lower. A ρ̂ at either end of the grid
(0 or 0.99) is flagged as a boundary solution. Intervals use the AR(1) fit's model-based covariance. The arm is
Gaussian only and runs in the Gaussian cells at
G = 100 with the OU (default signal), smooth (default signal), exact-AR(1), sign-changing, heteroskedastic and
misregistration (both truths) errors, and in the plasmode cells listed in @tbl-plasmode-ar1. Each fit costs
`r length(CONST$AR_RHO_GRID)` grid fits plus the refinement (@sec-timing). Mean ρ̂ per cell and the share of
boundary solutions are in @tbl-ar1-rho.

```{r ar1}
ar1_cells <- DESIGN$cell[!is.na(DESIGN$extra) & grepl("ar1", DESIGN$extra) | DESIGN$block %in% c("ar1_home", "warp_ar1")]
ar1_tab <- cov_wide(ar1_cells, c("mean", "beta"), c("reml_model", "reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2_bias", "ar1_model")) |>
  filter(!is.na(ar1_model)) |>
  select(-D, -basis, -family, -signal)
ar1_is <- W |>
  filter(contrast == "ar1 vs proposal: interval score", estimand %in% c("mean", "beta")) |>
  transmute(error, truth, estimand, `IS AR(1) / bias-aware NCV` = ci(ratio, ratio_lower, ratio_upper, 2))
ar1_mse <- W |>
  filter(contrast == "ar1 vs ncv: squared error", estimand %in% c("mean", "beta")) |>
  transmute(error, truth, estimand, `MSE AR(1) / NCV` = ci(ratio, ratio_lower, ratio_upper, 2))
ar1_full <- ar1_tab |> left_join(ar1_is, by = c("error", "truth", "estimand")) |> left_join(ar1_mse, by = c("error", "truth", "estimand")) |> pretty()
save_tab(ar1_full, "synthetic-ar1")
rho <- FITS |> filter(fit == "AR1") |> select(cell, error, truth, rho_mean, rho_boundary)
av <- \(a, err) ar1_tab[[a]][ar1_tab$error %in% err]
```

Modelling the dependence as AR(1) (ρ profiled) is conservative and competitive when the
errors are stationary and homoskedastic: coverage `r rng(av("ar1_model", c("ou", "fpc", "ou0", "osc")))`
on the OU, smooth, exact-AR(1) and sign-changing processes, with interval scores for β
`r rng(W$ratio[W$contrast == "ar1 vs proposal: interval score" & W$estimand == "beta" & W$error %in% c("ou", "fpc", "ou0", "osc")])`
times the bias-aware NCV interval's (@tbl-ar1). It fails under misregistration (mean
`r rng(ar1_tab$ar1_model[ar1_tab$error == "warp" & ar1_tab$estimand == "mean"])`, β
`r rng(ar1_tab$ar1_model[ar1_tab$error == "warp" & ar1_tab$estimand == "beta"])`; ρ̂ averages
`r rng(rho$rho_mean[rho$error == "warp"])`) and for γ(t) under covariate-dependent variance
(above). Fit times: median `r f(median(TIMING$fit_time[TIMING$method == "AR1"]), 0)` s per
AR(1) fit against `r f(median(TIMING$fit_time[TIMING$method == "REML"]), 1)` s (REML) and
`r f(median(TIMING$fit_time[TIMING$method == "NCV"]), 1)` s (NCV) plus about
`r f(median(TIMING$cl2_time, na.rm = TRUE), 1)` s per CL2 covariance, Gaussian G = 100 (10
replicates per error process).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ar1
#| tbl-cap: "AR(1) cells (Gaussian, G = 100): coverage, the interval-score ratio AR(1) / bias-aware NCV and the MSE ratio AR(1) / NCV, 95% bootstrap intervals."
show(ar1_full)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ar1-rho
#| tbl-cap: "AR(1) fits in the synthetic cells: mean profiled ρ̂ over replicates, share of replicates with ρ̂ at a grid end, and the median fit time."
show(FITS |> filter(fit == "AR1") |> transmute(cell, error = SHORT_ERROR[error], truth, `mean rho` = rho_mean, `boundary share` = rho_boundary, `median time s` = median_time) |> arrange(cell), digits = 3)
```
